key_insight: Finite-energy bosonic codes let one oscillator sense an external force while actively protecting an unknown logical qubit, with probe readout independent of the logical state.
engineering_relevance: The approach could combine force sensing and recoverable quantum memory in superconducting hardware without assigning them separate oscillator modes.
method: Encode logical amplitudes across discrete wave-packet sites.
Capture the force signal in a shared internal coordinate.
Use binomial site recovery to correct logical errors and packet-dependent probe distortions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports memory infidelity scaling as O(γ^(r+1)) and residual memory–probe correlations as O(γ^(r+2)) for a (2r+2)-packet code under photon loss γ, plus superconducting-circuit benchmarks.
watch_item: Photon-number dephasing and Kerr nonlinearity compete with photon-loss protection, making encoding choice hardware-dependent.
paper_title: Force Sensing in a Recoverable Bosonic Quantum Memory
